package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally published to npm to impersonate a legitimate local development example from React Native documentation. It collects a wide range of sensitive system and user information—including home directory, username, DNS servers, hostnames, internal and external IP addresses, organization, and package metadata—and exfiltrates this data to a hardcoded Discord webhook without user consent. This constitutes clear malicious data exfiltration and abuse of trust.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or during postinstall, the code collects sensitive system and user information (including home directory, username, DNS servers, hostnames, internal and external IP addresses, organization, and package metadata), serializes it as JSON, and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded Discord webhook, resulting in exfiltration of potentially sensitive developer and environment data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code systematically gathers a broad set of system and user information and transmits it to an external Discord webhook without any user notification, consent, or legitimate purpose. The use of a hardcoded webhook and the breadth of data collected are clear indicators of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package, especially one mimicking a documentation example, should not collect or transmit any user or system data externally. Normal behavior would be to provide only the documented functionality, without any telemetry or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect limited environment data, but only with explicit user consent, clear documentation, and opt-in mechanisms. They do not exfiltrate broad system information to hardcoded, third-party endpoints like Discord webhooks.
key_indicators: Collection of home directory, username, DNS servers, hostnames, and IP addresses
Use of hardcoded Discord webhook URL for data exfiltration
Execution at import-time or postinstall, before user code runs
No user notification, consent, or opt-in for telemetry
Impersonation of a documentation example to gain trust
Absence of legitimate package functionality (no real exports or README)

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious npm package named 'rtn-centered-text', matching the name of a local example from official React Native documentation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers are tricked into installing the malicious package via standard update or install commands, believing it to be a legitimate example.

attack_chain.action: Developer runs 'yarn upgrade rtn-centered-text' or similar commands, which fetch the malicious package from npm instead of using the intended local example.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is installed and becomes part of the developer's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in index.js executes at import-time or during postinstall, collecting sensitive system and user data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is aggregated and prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded Discord webhook endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive information from compromised developer environments.

behavioral_signatures: npm package that collects system, user, or network information at install or import time
Outbound HTTPS requests to Discord webhooks or other hardcoded endpoints during package installation or import
Impersonation of package names from official documentation examples to gain trust
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing code that imports 'os', 'dns', or other system/network modules
Presence of hardcoded Discord webhook URLs in source code
Absence of legitimate package functionality (e.g., missing README, no real exports, or only data exfiltration code)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Unexpected HTTPS POST requests to Discord domains during npm package install or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that collect and transmit environment or user data to external endpoints, especially during install or import. Flag packages containing hardcoded webhook URLs or those that match names of local development examples from documentation. Use static analysis to detect use of 'os', 'dns', and network modules in package entry points, and monitor for outbound requests to Discord or other suspicious domains during package installation. Correlate package names with known documentation examples to identify impersonation attempts.
